messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed on Dedicated cluster d-7 (us-east-2) — alerting SRE oncall. Severity: S2. Affected customer: HarborBridge.
Maya R: got the page, joining. tagging @Liam H for infra help. any customer-visible errors yet?
Liam H: seeing a spike of 503s from the gateway tier to d-7 backend pools. 503 rate ~18% over 1m, up from baseline 0.4%.
Esther P: I'm on chat with HarborBridge support. They're seeing failures for ingestion endpoints and some timeouts in their dashboard — reporting increased latency ~8s for batch uploads.
Nora S: copying their support logs now, ETA ~2m.
Maya R: ok plan: 1) confirm noisy tenant / capacity signal 2) if noisy tenant identified -> isolate and throttle 3) scale or failover traffic to spare capacity in other clusters 4) keep customer notified. Kai, can you surface KV eviction / GPU saturations?
Kai Z: looking at node-level metrics. Several hosts in d-7 have sustained 95-100% GPU utilization and high host-level load. KV evictions on the local cache increased ~430% last 10m. Patterns look like a single tenant issuing large prefix requests.
Liam H: on the serving side, we're seeing long tail P50->P99 token latencies jump. Logs show repeated long-running requests from tenant_id hb-tenant-987.
Maya R: that matches HarborBridge. Estimating noisy neighbor. Can we throttle that tenant at the routing layer as immediate mitigation?
Liam H: yep. Applying per-tenant rate limit on d-7 routing policy now: `rbac route update --cluster d-7 --tenant hb-tenant-987 --rate 50rps`
ops-bot: command accepted. Updated routing policy for hb-tenant-987 on d-7.
Maya R: push the throttle, confirm error reduction?
Liam H: throttle in place. within 60s 503% trending down. host GPU utilization dropping on nodes previously hot. KV evictions also declining.
Esther P: let me update HarborBridge: "we identified a noisy tenant pattern on d-7 and applied rate limiting; we expect improvements in 1-2m. Please keep sending examples if you see failures." They replied: "thanks, seeing fewer errors now but some retries still failing"
Nora S: collecting sample request ids. sending to SRE msgpack.
Maya R: good. Next: autoscale additional pool capacity to prevent recurrence while they backoff. Kai, can we spin up 2 additional workers in d-7 spare pool or failover to d-9?
Kai Z: d-7 autoscaler did not trigger because quota hit on reserved GPU capacity. We have spare in d-9 (same region) but need to update routing to allow cross-cluster failover. Will initiate gradual shift for non-latency-critical routes.
Liam H: initiating cross-cluster spill: `route-shift --from d-7 --to d-9 --selector non-realtime --pct 20 --duration 5m` starting now.
ops-bot: route-shift job started.
Maya R: Esther, let HarborBridge know we're spilling non-realtime traffic to d-9 and throttling heavy ingesters. Invite them to a short post-incident call.
Esther P: on it. Scheduled 30m postmortem with HarborBridge AMs.
Liam H: currently 5xx back to ~0.9% (from 18%). Gateway timeouts down to baseline. Monitoring P99s.
Maya R: great. root cause hypothesis: HarborBridge's internal tenant (hb-tenant-987) suddenly increased request concurrency and long-running prefix prompts, exhausting local KV caches and saturating GPUs -> KV evictions -> longer tail -> gateway 503s.
Kai Z: agree. Follow-ups: 1) enable tenant-level circuit breaker for long-running requests; 2) add protective per-tenant token concurrency caps; 3) refine autoscaler to account for sustained token-in-flight rather than just queue depth; 4) surface tenant burst alerts earlier.
Nora S: I've shared request samples and stack traces with SRE and Prod Eng.
Maya R: handoff: Liam, you're primary for the next 60m to stabilize and validate mitigation. Kai, can you own infra follow-ups (autoscale + failover runbook). Esther/Nora will keep coordinating with HarborBridge. I'll clear the page for now.
Liam H: ack, taking oncall. will open an incident ticket with timeline and mitigation steps.
ops-bot: incident ticket REDWOOD-INC-2026-486 created by Maya R.
Maya R: final note — no longer impacting SLAs for other customers; HarborBridge seeing degraded but improving UX. Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 11:00am. Closing thread when ticket is updated. :white_check_mark:
